industry.lead: Indian private hospitals are in a capacity boom backed by demand that is still growing: health-insurance premiums rose 15.4% to ₹1.4 lakh crore in FY26 (40.8% of non-life premiums), GST on retail health cover was cut from 18% to nil in Sep-2025, 43.5 crore Ayushman cards had been issued by Mar-2026, and the Medanta AR cites private hospital revenue growth of 16-18% a year with ARPOB growth of 6-8%. Listed operators are expected to add ~15,000 beds. For Medanta the tailwind is real but uneven: Tier-2 cities in UP and Bihar (Lucknow, Patna) have little high-end supply, while Delhi NCR, where Gurugram and Noida sit and two of the five new projects go (Mumbai is a third), is the most contested hospital market in India.
industry.src: AR FY26 MD&A pp. 66-68 (industry data as quoted there); Antique Stock Broking via Business Today (29-Jun-2026)
themes: Insurance penetration and GST cut on health cover
Insured patients pay for complex procedures; Medanta's TPA (cashless insurance) share is steady at ~25% of IP revenue, with 56% paid directly by patients.
CGHS rate revision (Oct-2025, first in years)
CGHS/ECHS/Railways is 10-12% of Medanta's IP revenue; management says the hike helps but does not move revenue 'by several hundred basis points'.
Tier-2 cities short of tertiary care (eastern UP, Bihar, Northeast)
Lucknow and Patna grew volumes 20%+ with no tariff increase; Guwahati (650 beds) targets patients who now travel out of the Northeast.
Hospital bed boom in NCR and metros
Noida, South Delhi, Pitampura and Mumbai enter markets where Max, Fortis, Apollo, Manipal and others are also adding beds; doctor costs rise first.
International revenue ₹278 cr in FY26 (+33%, 7% of revenue); Middle East flight disruptions hit Q4FY26; Bangladesh is still weak.
Low exposure today (no PM-JAY focus), but price caps on procedures or stents would hit a cardiac-heavy mix (heart ~21% of healthcare revenue).

ownership.peExits: Carlyle (Anant Investments) bought in 2013 and sold its entire stake (~5.07 crore shares) in the Nov-2022 IPO, as the company states; there is no Carlyle overhang. The remaining financial investor is Temasek (Dunearn), in since 2015: it sold ~3 million shares (~1.1%) in Feb-2024 at ~₹1,315 (RJ Corp bought ~2.88 million) and held 14.86% at Mar-2025 and 14.85% at Mar-2026, i.e. no sale in FY26. The 2026 supply came from co-founder Sunil Sachdeva: 10 lakh shares to HDFC MF in May-2026 (~₹122.5 cr) and 10 lakh in Jun-2026 (~₹130 cr, ~₹1,300 a share).

moat: Brand and clinical reputation
Strong advantage

Gurugram ranked India's best hospital in Newsweek's World's Best Hospitals 2026 (seven years in a row) and in the global top 110; JCI at Gurugram and Lucknow; founder Dr Trehan is among India's best-known cardiac surgeons.
Draws complex, high-paying cases from across North India and abroad (international 7% of revenue).
Clinical depth (department heads, 30+ specialties)
Advantage
2,480+ doctors; 550+ hired in FY26 and 70+ in Q1FY27 with 'negligible' senior attrition; transplant, robotics, oncology and cardiac programmes at scale.
Hard to copy quickly, but doctors are mobile and NCR rivals pay well.
Scale in under-served Tier-2 cities
Strong advantage
Lucknow (778 beds) and Patna (601) are the largest private hospitals in their states; 68-70% occupancy; 32% EBITDA margin with no tariff increase in Patna in 4.5 years.
First-mover position in markets of 100 million+ people; pricing power still unused.
Execution of greenfields
Advantage, proven three times
Lucknow and Patna broke even in their first full year; Noida's quarterly loss fell from ₹32 cr (Q3FY26) to ₹4.9 cr (Q1FY27).
Lowers the risk of the 2,950-bed pipeline, but four of five new projects are in costlier metros.
Cost position
Neutral
FY26 EBITDA margin (Screener basis) 21.1% vs 26.8% at Max, 22.8% at Fortis and 20.8% at Narayana; corporate costs sit in Gurugram; doctors' retainers 15% of revenue.
Medanta is not a low-cost operator; its margin depends on case mix.
Balance sheet
Advantage
Net cash ₹591 cr (company, Mar-2026) before leases; CRISIL AA/Stable.
Can fund most of ₹4,858 cr of capex with accruals plus modest debt.
Payer mix
Advantage
56% of IP revenue paid directly by patients, 25% cashless insurance, 11% CGHS/ECHS/Railways, almost no PM-JAY.
Protects realisations; insurers' price pressure is a slow-moving risk.
Concentration
Weakness
Cluster 1 (mostly Gurugram) was 63% of FY26 total income and growing ~10% a year; Gurugram is 15 years old and 'running quite full'.
Group growth now depends on Lucknow, Patna, Noida and the new projects.
critiques: The stock already prices the plan: the street pays 27-28x FY28E/Sep-28E EBITDA, above Medanta's own ~24x average of the last three years (Antique) and well above de-rated peers such as Narayana and Rainbow (~22-23x trailing).
Growth air pocket in FY29: the brownfield beds (418) are in by FY27-28 but none of the five greenfields (2,950 beds) opens before FY30 on management's own timeline, while ₹4,858 cr is spent.
Returns fall during the build: consolidated ROCE dropped from 18.1% to 14.9% in FY26 (company) and capex of ~₹1,000-1,300 cr a year will keep capital rising faster than profit until FY31.
FY26 EBITDA included ₹55.8 cr of EPCG grant income (₹16.2 cr in FY25), about 6% of EBITDA; it is tied to imports and export obligations, not to patients.
Metro entry is harder than Tier-2: Noida, South Delhi, Pitampura and Mumbai face entrenched competitors; the Lucknow/Patna playbook (no competition, no tariff increase needed) does not transfer.
Gurugram is maturing: Cluster 1 income grew 9% in FY26 and 10% in Q1FY27, with occupied bed-days flat in FY26; ARPOB (+10%) did the work.
Q4FY26 presentation p.20; Q1FY27 presentation p.15
Free float is thin and supply is real: promoter 33%, Temasek ~15%, co-founder ~10%, RJ Corp ~7%; the co-founder sold 0.74% in May-Jun 2026.
Bulls' answer: Noida breaks even early, Lucknow/Patna keep growing 20%+ with tariff headroom, and the balance sheet funds a near-doubling of beds; Medanta has executed every greenfield so far.
gaps: Noida's occupied bed-days, ARPOB and margin are not disclosed (only total income and EBITDA); management gave occupancy as '30% to 40%'. The bed build therefore models Noida inside Cluster 2.
Hospital-level (Gurugram vs Indore vs Ranchi; Lucknow vs Patna) revenue, beds and margins are not disclosed; only the two clusters.
Census beds by cluster are not disclosed; we derive them from occupied bed-days ÷ (days × occupancy), which reconciles to the network's 3,037 census beds in Q1FY27 within 0.2%.
Remaining capex by project: the Q1FY27 chart labels for Varanasi, medical college and guest house cannot be matched one to one; we show them together (₹561 cr).
Jun-2026 holdings of Dunearn (Temasek), Sunil Sachdeva and RJ Corp were not verified (Mar-2026 AR values used; Sachdeva's Jun-2026 stake estimated at ~10.0% after two 10-lakh-share blocks).
Quarterly grant (EPCG) income is not disclosed; FY27E assumes ₹30 cr for the year (GAM estimate).
Gross cash at Jun-2026 was not disclosed in the Q1 deck; other-income build uses Mar-2026 cash (₹1,222 cr, company).
Lease liabilities by hospital (which leases were added in FY26 for ₹216 cr) are not split out in the AR.
No consensus or broker note dated Sep-2026 was found; ICICI Securities, Emkay, Nuvama, Kotak and JPMorgan analysts asked questions on the calls, but their notes were not found.
Varanasi project capex and the lease liability it will add on commencement are not disclosed.
Exact opening years of Indore (2014) and Ranchi (2015) rest on the company timeline graphic; sources differ.
conflicts: The brief describes 'Carlyle-affiliated sell-downs'; the company states Carlyle (Anant Investments) exited completely in the Nov-2022 IPO. The remaining PE holder is Temasek (Dunearn, 14.85%), which did not sell in FY26. 2026 supply came from co-founder Sunil Sachdeva.

FY26 EBITDA: Screener ₹930 cr vs ₹919 cr from the AR P&L (after ESOP, before other income) vs company ₹1,056 cr (before ESOP, incl. other income). Screener shows ₹11 cr more finance cost (₹90 cr vs ₹79 cr). The model uses Screener (house rule); PL and Choice use ₹919 cr.
Screener's Jun-2025 quarter puts the ₹19.6 cr EPCG reversal inside operating profit (₹247 cr; ₹227 cr ex it), while its FY26 annual column treats it as exceptional.
Guwahati capex: the call gives a total project cost of ~₹970 cr; the deck's remaining capex is ₹904 cr (some land and early costs already spent).
Payor mix: the deck's 'cash' (56%) is by payment type; insurance reimbursed after discharge may sit in it, so cash and insurance shares are not comparable with peers that classify by payer.
